title: Chapter 1 Quiz: Hygiene Heroes
subtitle: 5-Question Wellness Wizard Check · Handwashing, Brushing & Clean Water

questions.question: How long should you scrub your hands with soap and water to remove germs effectively?
questions.explanation: CDC and WHO guidelines recommend scrubbing with soap and water for at least 20 seconds—about as long as humming 'Happy Birthday' twice!
questions.hint: Think about humming a short song twice while making soapy bubbles.

questions.question: Which parts of your hands are easy to miss and need extra care when washing?
options: Only the middle of your palms
Thumbs, between fingers, backs of hands, and fingertips
questions.explanation: Scrubbing palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs, and fingertips makes sure no hidden germs stay behind.
questions.hint: Remember all 5 zones you scrubbed at the Town Square fountain!

questions.question: How often and how long should you brush your teeth each day?
options: Twice a day for 2 minutes with fluoride toothpaste
questions.explanation: Brushing twice a day for 2 minutes sweeps away plaque and protects tooth enamel.
questions.hint: Two times a day, two minutes each time!

questions.question: If clear-looking water comes from an outdoor pond or uncovered bucket, is it automatically safe to drink?
options: Yes, if it looks clear it has no germs
No, invisible germs can live in clear water—it must be treated or boiled
Yes, as long as it smells okay
questions.explanation: Microscopic germs are invisible! Safe drinking water comes from tested clean taps or properly boiled/filtered water.
questions.hint: Can our bare eyes see tiny bacteria or parasites?

questions.question: What should you do if you have a persistent toothache?
options: Ignore it and chew hard candy
Tell a trusted adult so you can see a dentist
questions.explanation: Telling a trusted adult or dentist early helps fix toothaches gently and keeps your mouth healthy.
questions.hint: Who helps us check sore teeth safely?

title: Chapter 2 Quiz: Nutrition Navigators
subtitle: 5-Question Wellness Wizard Check · Balanced Plates, Labels & Food Groups

questions.question: What does 'eating a rainbow' on your plate help your body get?
options: A wide mix of vitamins, minerals, and fiber from colorful fruits and veggies
questions.explanation: Each fruit and vegetable color brings different helpful nutrients that support eyes, skin, energy, and immunity!
questions.hint: Think about why red berries, orange carrots, and green spinach are all helpful.

questions.question: Which drink is the best everyday choice to keep your body hydrated without added sugar?
questions.explanation: Water refreshes your body, supports focus, and hydrates without sneaky added sugars.
questions.hint: It's clear, refreshing, and flows freely in Sunnybrook!

questions.question: On an ingredient label, which of these words can signal hidden added sugar?
options: High-fructose corn syrup or cane syrup
questions.explanation: Words ending in '-ose' or 'syrup' often indicate added sugars tucked inside packaged snacks.
questions.hint: Look for sweet syrups hidden in ingredient lists.

questions.question: Which food group provides building blocks to help muscles grow and repair?
options: Protein foods like beans, eggs, fish, nuts, and poultry
questions.explanation: Proteins supply amino acids that help build and repair muscles, skin, and tissues.
questions.hint: Farmer Fig stores beans, nuts, and eggs in this basket!

questions.question: Why are whole grains like brown rice and oatmeal great for school and play?
options: They give steady, lasting energy plus helpful fiber
They make you sleepy right away
questions.explanation: Whole grains release energy gradually so you feel fueled and focused instead of crashing.
questions.hint: Think about steady fuel vs. a quick sugar rush.

title: Chapter 3 Quiz: Fitness Trailblazers
subtitle: 5-Question Wellness Wizard Check · Daily Movement, Warm-Ups & Hydration

questions.question: About how much fun physical activity do kids and teens benefit from each day?
options: About 60 minutes a day of active play, walking, or sports
questions.explanation: WHO and CDC guidelines recommend around 60 minutes daily of enjoyable moderate-to-vigorous movement for ages 5–17.
questions.hint: One full hour of active play, biking, dancing, or walking!

questions.question: Why is a gentle warm-up helpful before running or playing sports?
options: It wakes up muscles and joints gradually to help prevent strains
It uses up all your water
questions.explanation: Gentle marching and dynamic stretches warm muscles safely so your body moves smoothly.
questions.hint: Remember Coach Kiko's Stretch It Out lesson!

questions.question: What should you do during active play or hiking on a sunny day?
options: Take water breaks and listen to your body
questions.explanation: Regular sips of water replace fluids lost through sweat and keep your energy steady.
questions.hint: Check what helped along Sunnybrook Trail!

questions.question: Which of these counts as healthy exercise?
options: Dancing, riding a bike, walking the dog, or playing tag
questions.explanation: Any joyful movement that gets your heart beating faster—dancing, biking, walking, or tag—counts!
questions.hint: Exercise works best when it's fun!

questions.question: If you ever feel dizzy or feel sharp pain while exercising, what is the smartest move?
options: Stop, rest, drink water, and tell a coach or trusted adult
questions.explanation: Listening to your body and telling a trusted adult keeps play safe and fun.
questions.hint: Safety always comes before finishing a race!

title: Chapter 4 Quiz: Rest & Calm Keepers
subtitle: 5-Question Wellness Wizard Check · Sleep Routines & Mental Wellness

questions.question: About how many hours of sleep do kids ages 8–12 need each night to recharge?
questions.explanation: Kids ages 6–12 generally need 9–12 hours of sleep (and teens 8–10 hours) to grow, learn, and feel rested.
questions.hint: Almost half of a 24-hour day—between 9 and 12 hours!

questions.question: Why is turning off bright screens 30–60 minutes before bed helpful?
options: Bright blue light can trick your brain into thinking it's still daytime
questions.explanation: Dimming screens lets your brain produce sleepy melatonin naturally so you fall asleep easier.
questions.hint: Think about what Granny Luna taught Sleepy Sam.

questions.question: How can slow belly breathing help when you feel worried or overwhelmed?
options: It signals your body to slow your heart rate and calm down
questions.explanation: Slow deep breaths calm the nervous system and help stressful thoughts settle.
questions.hint: Remember clearing the Worry Clouds by the hearth!

questions.question: What happens in your body while you sleep deeply?
options: Your brain organizes memories and your body repairs and grows
Your muscles forget how to move
questions.explanation: Sleep is active repair time for both brain and body!
questions.hint: Rest helps you wake up sharper and stronger.

questions.question: If big worries keep bothering you day after day, what is a healthy thing to do?
options: Talk with a trusted adult, parent, teacher, or counselor
questions.explanation: Sharing big feelings with a trusted adult connects you with real support and care.
questions.hint: You never have to carry heavy worries alone.

title: Chapter 5 Quiz: Prevention Protectors
subtitle: 5-Question Wellness Wizard Check · Germs, Etiquette, Vaccines & Mosquito Patrol

questions.question: What is the cleanest way to catch a sudden cough or sneeze if you don't have a tissue?
questions.explanation: Sneezing into your elbow keeps droplets out of the air and off your hands!
questions.hint: Teacher Tam called it the 'vampire sneeze'!

questions.question: Why should shared spots like doorknobs and classroom desks be wiped clean regularly?
options: Many hands touch them, so germs can transfer from person to person
questions.explanation: High-touch surfaces can carry germs between hands—routine cleaning plus handwashing stops the chain.
questions.hint: Think about what glowed under your Germ Goggles!

questions.question: How do vaccines help protect your body?
options: They safely train your immune system to recognize a germ before it makes you sick
questions.explanation: Vaccines give your Immune Team a safe practice drill so it remembers how to defend you quickly!
questions.hint: Remember Nurse Nora's Immune Team training shield!

questions.question: Why did Nurse Nora ask you to empty standing water from buckets and flowerpots?
options: Mosquitoes lay eggs in still water—emptying them prevents mosquito-borne illness
questions.explanation: Removing stagnant water eliminates mosquito breeding grounds near homes and schools.
questions.hint: Where do mosquito larvae grow?

questions.question: If you feel sick with a fever or questions about medicine, who should you ask?
questions.explanation: Always check with a trusted adult or healthcare professional when you feel sick or have medical questions.
questions.hint: Sunnybrook's golden safety rule!
